37469-some-imagist-poets-1916-an-annual-.creator: Unknown
37469-some-imagist-poets-1916-an-annual-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The authors wish to express their gratitude to the editors of _The Egoist_ and _Poetry and Drama_, London; _The Poetry Journal_, Boston; _The Little Review_ and _Poetry_, Chicago, for permission to reprint certain of these poems which originally appeared in their columns.

arxiv-1604-00123.title: Higgs exotic decays in general NMSSM with self-interacting dark matter
arxiv-1604-00123.creator: Wenyu Wang 1, Mengchao Zhang 2, Jun Zhao 1,2
arxiv-1604-00123.description: Abstract Under current LHC and dark matter constraints, the general NMSSM can have self-interacting dark matter to explain the cosmological small structure. In this scenario, the dark matter is the light singlino-like neutralino ( χ \chi ) which self-interacts through exchanging the light singlet-like scalars ( h 1 , a 1 h_{1},a_{1} ).

arxiv-2105-04106.title: Validation of image systems simulation technology using a Cornell Box
arxiv-2105-04106.creator: Zheng Lyu, Krithin Kripakaran, Max Furth, Eric Tang, Brian Wandell, Joyce Farrell
arxiv-2105-04106.description: Abstract We describe and experimentally validate an end-to-end simulation of a digital camera. The simulation models the spectral radiance of 3D-scenes, formation of the spectral irradiance by multi-element optics, and conversion of the irradiance to digital values by the image sensor.

arxiv-2205-05245.title: Salient Object Detection via Bounding-box Supervision
arxiv-2205-05245.creator: Mengqi He, Jing Zhang, Wenxin Yu
arxiv-2205-05245.description: Abstract The success of fully supervised saliency detection models depends on a large number of pixel-wise labeling. In this paper, we work on bounding-box based weakly-supervised saliency detection to relief the labeling effort. Given the bounding box annotation, we observe that pixels inside the bounding box may contains extensive labeling noise.

arxiv-2302-11703.title: fAIlureNotes: Supporting Designers in Understanding the Limits of AI Models for Computer Vision Tasks Conference: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 23–28, 2023; Hamburg, Germany Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Sys
arxiv-2302-11703.creator: Steven Moore, Q. Vera Liao, Hariharan Subramonyam
arxiv-2302-11703.description: Abstract . To design with AI models, user experience (UX) designers must assess the fit between the model and user needs. Based on user research, they need to contextualize the model’s behavior and potential failures within their product-specific data instances and user scenarios.

arxiv-2304-13682.title: Measured foliations at infinity and CMC foliations of quasi-Fuchsian manifolds close to the Fuchsian locus
arxiv-2304-13682.creator: Diptaishik Choudhury
arxiv-2304-13682.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Diptaishik Choudhury. The main subject of this thesis are a certain class of hyperbolic 3 3 -manifolds called quasi-Fuchsian manifold. Given an orientied, closed hyperbolic surface S S , these manifolds are homeomorphic to S × ℝ S\times\mathbb{R} . We study two questions regarding them: one is on measured foliations at infinity and the other is on foliation by constant mean curvature surfaces .

arxiv-2405-01089.title: Probing the structure of X ⁡ ( 3872 ) X(3872) in photoproduction
arxiv-2405-01089.creator: E. Ya. Paryev
arxiv-2405-01089.description: Abstract We study the production of X ⁡ ( 3872 ) X(3872) mesons in photon-induced nuclear reactions near the threshold within the collision model based on the nuclear spectral function. The model accounts for direct photon-nucleon X ⁡ ( 3872 ) X(3872) production processes as well as five different scenarios for their internal structure.

arxiv-2411-02883.title: Analysis of discrete modern Hopfield networks in open quantum system
arxiv-2411-02883.creator: Takeshi Kimura 1, Kohtaro Kato 1
arxiv-2411-02883.description: Abstract The modern Hopfield network, proposed by Krotov and Hopfield, is a mathematical generalization of the Hopfield network, which is a basic model of associative memory that employs higher-order interactions. This study introduces an open quantum model for discrete modern Hopfield networks that generalizes the open quantum Hopfield network.

arxiv-2411-06304.title: Widespread neuronal chaos induced by slow oscillating currents
arxiv-2411-06304.creator: James Scully, Carter Hinsley, David Bloom, Hil G.E. Meijer, Andrey L. Shilnikov
arxiv-2411-06304.description: Abstract This paper investigates the origin and onset of chaos in a mathematical model of an individual neuron, arising from the intricate interaction between 3D fast and 2D slow dynamics governing its intrinsic currents. Central to the chaotic dynamics are multiple homoclinic connections and bifurcations of saddle equilibria and periodic orbits.

arxiv-2412-18850.title: Dynamics of Topological Defects in a Rashba Spin-Orbit Coupled Bose-Einstein Condensate
arxiv-2412-18850.creator: Sheng Liu, Yong-Sheng Zhang
arxiv-2412-18850.description: Abstract We investigate the quench dynamics of a two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensate. Our study focuses on quenching the system from a zero-momentum phase to a plane-wave phase. During this quench, topological defects emerge in the form of vortices. These vortices and anti-vortices exhibit a random spatial distribution with equal numbers, mirroring the core principles of Kosterlitz-Thouless physics.

arxiv-2504-18498.title: Enhancing Visual Interpretability and Explainability in Functional Survival Trees and Forests
arxiv-2504-18498.creator: Giuseppe Loffredo* \affilnum 1, Elvira Romano \affilnum 1 and Fabrizio Maturo \affilnum 2
arxiv-2504-18498.description: Abstract Functional survival models are key tools for analyzing time-to-event data with complex predictors, such as functional or high-dimensional inputs. Despite their predictive strength, these models often lack interpretability, which limits their value in practical decision-making and risk analysis. This study investigates two key survival models: the Functional Survival Tree (FST) and the Functional Random Survival Forest (FRSF).

arxiv-2506-18104.title: Enhancing VICReg: Random-Walk Pairing for Improved Generalization and Better Global Semantics Capturing
arxiv-2506-18104.creator: Idan Simai, Ronen Talmon, Uri Shaham
arxiv-2506-18104.description: Abstract In this paper, we argue that viewing VICReg-a popular self-supervised learning (SSL) method–through the lens of spectral embedding reveals a potential source of sub-optimality: it may struggle to generalize robustly to unseen data due to overreliance on the training data.

arxiv-2509-03091.title: Diffusive shock acceleration: non-classical model of cosmic ray transport
arxiv-2509-03091.description: Abstract In this work the theory of diffusive shock acceleration is extended to the case of non-classical particle transport with Lévy flights and Lévy traps, when the mean square displacement grows nonlinearly with time. In this approach the Green function is not a Gaussian but it exhibits power-law tails.

arxiv-2509-24650.title: VoxCPM: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Context-Aware Speech Generation and True-to-Life Voice Cloning
arxiv-2509-24650.description: Abstract Generative models for speech synthesis face a fundamental trade-off: discrete tokens ensure stability but sacrifice expressivity, while continuous signals retain acoustic richness but suffer from error accumulation due to task entanglement. This challenge has driven the field towards multi-stage pipelines that rely on pre-trained speech tokenizers, but these create a semantic-acoustic divide, limiting holistic and expressive speech generation.

arxiv-2512-22991.title: Fusion or Confusion? Multimodal Complexity Is Not All You Need
arxiv-2512-22991.creator: Tillmann Rheude, Roland Eils, Benjamin Wild
arxiv-2512-22991.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tillmann Rheude, Roland Eils, Benjamin Wild. Deep learning architectures for multimodal learning have increased in complexity, driven by the assumption that multimodal-specific methods improve performance. We challenge this assumption through a large-scale empirical study reimplementing 19 19 high-impact methods under standardized conditions, evaluating them across nine diverse datasets with up to 23 23 modalities, and testing their generalizability to new tasks beyond their original scope, including settings with missing modalities.

arxiv-2601-08365.title: Impacted Buildings for GL ⁡ ( 2 ) \GL(2) Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2601-08365.creator: Malors Espinosa, Zander Karaganis
arxiv-2601-08365.description: Abstract In this paper we define a generating function for buildings of type A ~ 1 \widetilde{A}_{1} (i.e. trees) that are enhanced with a certain filtration structure. We prove that this generating function recovers the zeta function of certain quadratic orders.

pmc-11634560.title: Identification of Chronic Hypertension in Pregnancy in Three Administrative Data Sources Among Medicaid‐Funded Births in California
pmc-11634560.creator: Erin Delker, Rebecca J Baer, Christina D Chambers, Gretchen Bandoli
pmc-11634560.description: PurposeAdministrative data sources are used to describe the epidemiology of chronic hypertension in pregnancy and its consequences. Differences in identification across sources may affect research estimates. We compared identification of chronic hypertension in birth certificate records, hospital discharge records, and Medi‐Cal claims in the same individuals.MethodsWe used data from 820 140 2016–2020 California Medi‐Cal covered births.

pmc-11662637.title: National Survey on the Management of Genital Prolapse in Italy
pmc-11662637.creator: Matteo Frigerio, Andrea Morciano, Marta Barba, Michele Carlo Schiavi, Alice Cola, Elena Cavaliere, Carlo Rappa, Mauro Cervigni, On behalf of the “Young Commission” of the Italian Association of Urological Gynecology and Pelvic Floor (AIUG)
pmc-11662637.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeSurgical repair is considered the mainstay of genital prolapse management. Several procedures are available both by vaginal and abdominal route, with and without mesh augmentation. The Italian UroGynecology Association (AIUG) promoted this survey with the aim of evaluating current variations in the surgical management of various types of prolapse in different clinical settings and to compare practice amongst practitioners working in high- and medium/low-volume centers.Participants and MethodsThe questionnaire examined four contentious areas of contemporary prolapse management.

pmc-11678186.title: Aortitis Increases the Risk of Surgical Complications and Re-Operations After Major Aortic Surgery
pmc-11678186.creator: Edward Staniforth, Shirish Dubey, Iakovos Ttofi, Vanitha Perinparajah, Jasmina Ttofi, Rohit Vijjhalwar, Raman Uberoi, Ediri Sideso, George Krasopoulos, Alan P Sawchuk
pmc-11678186.description: Aortitis, defined as inflammation of the aorta, can lead to aneurysms and dissections. Intra-operative sampling is essential for diagnosis, with many cases presenting asymptomatically as clinically isolated aortitis. Previous studies investigating aortitis in major aortic surgery have been limited by low intra-operative sampling.

pmc-12472174.title: Serum Indoxyl Sulfate as a Potential Biomarker of Aortic Stiffness in Persons with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-12472174.creator: I-Min Su, Yi-Yen Teng, Jer-Chuan Li, Chin-Hung Liu, Du-An Wu, Bang-Gee Hsu
pmc-12472174.description: Background and Objectives: Indoxyl sulfate (IS), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite of tryptophan, is implicated in vascular dysfunction through oxidative stress and inflammation. This study evaluated the association between serum IS levels and aortic stiffness (AS) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

pmc-12563799.title: Feasibility of a Physiatry Assessment Clinic to Address Physical Impairment in Head and Neck Cancer Patients Following Neck Resection and Free Flap Reconstruction
pmc-12563799.creator: Lauren C Capozzi, Chad Wagoner, Julia T Daun, Lisa Murphy, Steven C Nakoneshny, George J Francis, Joseph C Dort, Khara Sauro, S Nicole Culos-Reed
pmc-12563799.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryIndividuals with head and neck cancer are living longer than ever before, yet due to intensive treatments including surgery, many live with long-term side effects impacting their function and quality of life. A growing body of evidence supports the role of early rehabilitation in improving patient outcomes; however, the optimal timing and implementation of rehabilitation services have not been established. This study assessed the feasibility of a physiatry assessment clinic approximately two months postoperatively.

pmc-12623026.title: Regional Brain Structure Alterations in Diabetes but Not Prediabetes
pmc-12623026.creator: Liangqi Wang, Huandong Lin, Zehua Zhao, Lingyan Chen, Li Wu, Ting Liu, Jing Li, Chu-Chung Huang, Chun-Yi Zac Lo, Xin Gao
pmc-12623026.description: ContextDiabetes (DM) affects brain volume and white matter hyperintensity (WMH), but whether regional gray matter volume (GMV) and tract-specific WMH progress in the prediabetes (PreDM) stage remains unclear.ObjectiveWe investigate brain structural changes across 3 distinct glycemic states.MethodsWe analyzed 512 participants (122 with DM, 109 with PreDM, and 281 controls) using advanced neuroimaging techniques.

pmc-12654198.title: Foot Traffic Driven Anthropogenic Activity Alters Phyllosphere Microbial Community Characteristics and Putative Pathogens in Subtropical Urban Green Spaces
pmc-12654198.creator: Abdul Baess Keyhani, Wei He, Mingjun Teng, Zhaogui Yan, Monira Fayaz, Zhaohui Peng, Yangyang Zhang, Safir Ahmad Tamim, Xiuyuan Wang, Zemin Han, Pujie Wei, Lei Pan, Pengcheng Wang
pmc-12654198.description: Green spaces in subtropical cities are important for providing ecological services that support human well-being and serve as reservoirs for diverse microbial communities, which in turn support ecosystem functions. However, studies on the characteristics of the phyllosphere microbial community and public health risks associated with putative pathogens in various urban green spaces exposed to anthropogenic stress remain limited.

pmc-12979723.title: A single-arm phase Ib study of personalized peptide-pulsed dendritic cell-based multiple target cytotoxic T lymphocyte immunotherapy in combination with toripalimab as second-line therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
pmc-12979723.creator: Weihong Zhang, Jing Qin, Jing Luo, Yanjuan Xiong, Fan Yang, Bin Li, Meng Shen, Huizhen Geng, Zibo Li, Xiao Tian, Shuzhan Li, Runmei Li, Yang Wang, Xinwei Zhang, Xiubao Ren, Qian Sun, Li Zhou, Liang Liu
pmc-12979723.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAnti-programmed cell death 1 (PD-1)/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) monoclonal antibody therapy has been approved as second-line treatment for advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Unfortunately, the objective response rate (ORR) is not satisfied. T lymphocytes obtained by co-culture with personalized tumor-specific antigenic peptide-pulsed dendritic cells (DC), also known as multiple target cytotoxic T lymphocytes (MCTL) can restore the antitumor immunity and potentially improve clinical outcomes.

pmc-13188609.title: Evaluating function availability and user satisfaction with nutrition apps: user-generated content analysis and text mining study
pmc-13188609.creator: Songping Li, Qinghua Yao, Feihe Shao, Kejun Yang, Xiao Yu, Lixue Zhou, Junyi Xin
